Rules:
1. Answer with exactly one read-only SELECT statement (a WITH clause is allowed) inside a ```sql code block, and nothing after it.
2. If the database cannot answer the question, reply with exactly one line: -- UNANSWERABLE: <short reason>
3. If the question is too vague to answer without guessing, reply with exactly one line: -- CLARIFY: <the question you need answered>
4. Use the dates named in the question. Do not use NOW() or CURDATE(). For reference, the data runs up to 2026-10-31.

Schema (the tables most likely to be needed):
code_lookup - Meaning of every coded column in the other tables: code_type (which code list: ORD_STATUS, TIER, REFUND_STATUS, REFUND_REASON, TKT_CATEG, REGION, CHANNEL, DEPT); code_val (the stored code); code_desc (what the code means in words)
cust_master - Customer master record: cust_id (customer id, like C-1002); cust_nm (customer name); tier_cd (loyalty tier: P platinum, G gold, S standard); region_cd (sales region: NA, EU, AP, LA); signup_dt (date the customer signed up); is_actv (1 = active, 0 = closed or inactive (soft delete)); email_addr (contact email address); phone_no (contact phone number)
prod_catalog - Product catalog: sku (stock keeping unit); prod_nm (product name); categ_cd (product category code: KIT kitchen, HOM home, OFC office, ELC electronics); list_prc (list price in USD); disc_flag (1 = product is DISCONTINUED (not a price discount), 0 = still sold)
policy_rule - Policy values that change over time; pick the row in force on the date you care about: rule_id (rule row id); rule_key (which policy: refund_approval_threshold (USD amount above which a refund needs manager approval), sla_hours_sev1 (hours to resolve a critical ticket)); rule_val (the value, stored as text); eff_from (first date the value applies); eff_to (last date the value applies; NULL = still in force)
supplier - Suppliers: sup_id (supplier id); sup_nm (supplier name); country (two letter country code)
prod_supplier - Which suppliers provide which products: sku (product); sup_id (supplier that can provide it); lead_days (days from ordering to receiving); is_primary (1 = the main supplier for this product)  FK: sku->prod_catalog.sku, sup_id->supplier.sup_id
Show the supplier name, product SKU, and lead days for suppliers whose lead time is strictly greater than the average lead time of all primary supplier records.

```sql
SELECT T2.sup_nm, T1.sku, T1.lead_days FROM prod_supplier AS T1 JOIN supplier AS T2 ON T1.sup_id = T2.sup_id WHERE T1.lead_days > (SELECT AVG(lead_days) FROM prod_supplier WHERE is_primary = 1) ORDER BY T1.lead_days DESC, T2.sup_nm ASC, T1.sku ASC
```

Find the customer name, order ID, order total amount, and promotion name for orders placed in April 2026 that applied a promotion, sorted by order total descending.

```sql
SELECT c.cust_nm, o.ord_id, o.ord_total_amt, p.promo_nm FROM ord_hdr o JOIN cust_master c ON o.cust_id = c.cust_id JOIN ord_promo op ON o.ord_id = op.ord_id JOIN promo p ON op.promo_id = p.promo_id WHERE o.ord_dt >= '2026-04-01' AND o.ord_dt <= '2026-04-30' ORDER BY o.ord_total_amt DESC, o.ord_id ASC
```



A fragile supply chain product is any product where the single primary supplier has a lead time exceeding 25 days. Show the SKU, product name, supplier name, and lead days for all fragile supply chain products, ordered by lead days descending, breaking ties by SKU ascending.

```sql
SELECT p.sku, p.prod_nm, s.sup_nm, ps.lead_days FROM prod_catalog p JOIN prod_supplier ps ON p.sku = ps.sku JOIN supplier s ON ps.sup_id = s.sup_id WHERE ps.is_primary = 1 AND ps.lead_days > 25 ORDER BY ps.lead_days DESC, p.sku ASC
```


Show the warehouse name and the total positive stock movements (IN) recorded at each warehouse during October 2025, highest total quantity first.

For each customer tier, display the tier code, total number of orders placed in 2026, count of orders with status 'N' (new), count of orders with status 'S' (shipped), and the percentage of shipped orders among all orders. Order by tier code ascending.

```sql
SELECT t2.tier_cd, COUNT(t1.ord_id) AS total_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.ord_status = 'N' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS new_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.ord_status = 'S' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shipped_orders, (SUM(CASE WHEN t1.ord_status = 'S' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / COUNT(t1.ord_id) AS shipped_pct FROM ord_hdr AS t1 JOIN cust_master AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND t1.ord_dt <= '2026-12-31' GROUP BY t2.tier_cd ORDER BY t2.tier_cd ASC
```

```sql

```

For each warehouse name, compute the total inventory on-hand quantity, the total reorder point sum, and the ratio of total on-hand quantity to total reorder point expressed as a percentage.

```sql
SELECT w.wh_nm, SUM(i.on_hand_qty) AS total_on_hand, SUM(i.reorder_pt) AS total_reorder_pt, (SUM(i.on_hand_qty) * 100.0) / NULLIF(SUM(i.reorder_pt), 0) AS stock_to_reorder_ratio FROM warehouse w JOIN inventory i ON w.wh_id = i.wh_id GROUP BY w.wh_id, w.wh_nm ORDER BY w.wh_nm ASC
```

```sql

```

